title: Algebraization of a principal-adic finite-type quotient tower
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $a\in A$. For each $m\geq1$ let $C_m$ be a finite type commutative $A/(a^m)$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with $A$-algebra transition maps $t_m:C_m\to C_{m-1}$ for $m\geq2$. Assume that each $t_m$ induces an isomorphism $C_m/a^{m-1}C_m\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{m-1}$. Then $F=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}C_m$, with componentwise ring operations, is an $(a)$-adically complete Noetherian $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every $m$, its coordinate projection induces an $A$-algebra isomorphism $F/a^mF\xrightarrow{\sim}C_m$, compatible with transitions. There are $q\geq0$ and an ideal $Q$ of $\widehat{A[z_1,\ldots,z_q]}_{(a)}$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with an $A$-algebra isomorphism $F\cong\widehat{A[z_1,\ldots,z_q]}_{(a)}/Q$.

source.place: Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type), quasi-inverse for the category in equation-C and its completed polynomial presentation; Tag 0AJQ (lemma-topologically-finite-type-Noetherian), part (1), for Noetherianity.

proof.text: Put $I=(a)\subset A$ and regard each $C_m$ as an $A/I^m$-module. The transition isomorphisms in the hypothesis are also module isomorphisms, and $I$ is generated by the single element $a$. Apply [lem-pod-adic-tower-reconstruction] to obtain completeness and separatedness of $F$ and bijections $F/a^mF\to C_m$ induced by the projections. The projections preserve $1$, sums, products and the $A$-action, since these operations on compatible sequences are componentwise; thus the bijections are $A$-algebra isomorphisms. For $m\ge2$, $t_m\operatorname{pr}_m=\operatorname{pr}_{m-1}$ by the definition of $F$, proving the required compatibility of all quotient isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type), first proof paragraph, applying Algebra Tag 09B8 (lemma-limit-complete).

proof.text: The isomorphism $F/aF\cong C_1$ and finite type of $C_1$ give a finite list of algebra generators over $A/(a)$. Lift these through the surjective projection $F\to C_1$ to $b_1,\ldots,b_q\in F$, allowing $q=0$. Let $R=A[z_1,\ldots,z_q]$. The polynomial universal property gives the $A$-algebra map $e:R\to F$, $z_i\mapsto b_i$. Every residue in $F/aF$ is a polynomial in these residues with coefficients in $A/(a)$, whose coefficients lift to $A$. Consequently $R\xrightarrow e F\to F/aF$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type), final proof paragraph: choose generators of the closed fibre and lift them.

proof.text: Set $P=\widehat R_{(a)}=\varprojlim_mR/a^mR$. For the base ring $R$ and its principal ideal $(a)$, the module tower $R/a^mR$ has the required transition quotients: dividing $R/a^{m+1}R$ by the image of $a^mR$ is exactly $R/a^mR$. Thus [lem-pod-adic-tower-reconstruction] makes $P$ $(a)$-adically complete. Since $e(a^mr)=a^me(r)$, $e$ induces $e_m:R/a^mR\to F/a^mF$. These maps commute with reduction, because both composites send the class of $r$ to the class of $e(r)$. For $x=(x_m)_m\in P$, the compatible sequence $(e_m(x_m))_m$ therefore determines a unique element $\phi(x)\in F$ by completeness of $F$ from Step 1. Coordinatewise sums, products, $1$ and constants show that $\phi:P\to F$ is an $A$-algebra homomorphism and extends $e$.

source.place: Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type), completed polynomial ring and extension of evaluation in the final proof paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] with source $P$, target $F$, ideal $J=aP$ and map $\phi$. The source is $J$-adically complete, hence precomplete, by Step 3. The extended ideal $JF=aF$, since $J$ is generated by $a$ and $\phi$ is an $A$-algebra map. The target is $aF$-adically Hausdorff by Step 1. Finally $P\to F/aF$ is surjective: its restriction along $R\to P$ is the surjective map of Step 2. All hypotheses of the cited criterion hold, so $\phi$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type), final surjectivity argument using Algebra Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities), part (1); existing complete-source criterion is its successive-approximation form.

proof.text: Let $Q=\ker\phi\subset P$. The map $P/Q\to F$, $[p]\mapsto\phi(p)$, is well-defined and preserves the $A$-algebra operations. It is injective because $\phi(p)=\phi(p')$ is equivalent to $p-p'\in Q$, and surjective by Step 4. Its inverse is therefore the $A$-algebra isomorphism $F\cong P/Q$ asserted in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type), quotient presentation obtained from the surjective completed evaluation.

proof.text: The algebra $R=A[z_1,\ldots,z_q]$ is finite type: its displayed variables generate it, including the empty list when $q=0$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] gives that $R$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] to $R$ and its ideal $(a)$ to conclude that $P$ is Noetherian. The surjection $\phi:P\to F$ and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] now imply that $F$ is Noetherian. Together with Steps 1 and 5 this proves every assertion.

source.place: Tag 0AJQ (lemma-topologically-finite-type-Noetherian), proof of part (1), using Algebra Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian).
